pilot.summary: First game ever with the deck, a pod of three at home against Stuart (zombie tokens) and Steven (card draw and counterspells). Sol Ring in the opener got it going fast, and a late wheel made Shabraz big enough that I almost killed Stuart with commander damage. Then it went grindy. Brallin got removed twice and picked up tax, no more ramp showed up, and I had no removal for the board or answer to Steven's counters. No result was logged.

A loss at Oliver's, the second game of the night, against Oliver, Tom and Ryan. I mulliganed into a hand with one playable creature and a bunch of wheels and wasn't sure I should have kept it. The Shabraz wheels went well. My main finding was that the list ran too many wheels. They should be finishers, held until both commanders are out and big, partly because the table doesn't like discarding its hand over and over.

A short note on the first game with the voltron list, v2.0.0. It was slow: no removal, slow to get cards out, and mana starved for a round. I couldn't tell if it was sequencing or the cards I saw. No result or table was logged.

A loss at Ryan's house to Alex's warp deck, which ramps to around 15 mana and keeps its warped creatures with an artifact that ends the turn. Ryan was on Slivers. The draw/discard engine ran well and Smothering Tithe made steady Treasure, but I kept a land-and-ramp hand with one wheel, held both commanders back waiting for a wheel that never came, and got outpaced. The rule since is to cast the first commander on curve.

A late three-player loss at my house. Alex played my Goblin Storm and won on Purphoros pings, and David was on golems. I kept a ramp-heavy hand again, got Marauding Mako to +6/+6 off a wheel, but never got a commander out. I put it on piloting: I got distracted by the small discard creatures instead of building toward the commanders.

Second game of a five-player night at Oliver's, at a table that had stepped up to bracket 4. Ryan's T'Vol went infinite around turn 8-9 and won. I had Shabraz, Brallin, Fiery Emancipation, Smothering Tithe with 36 Treasure, Mystic Remora and Teferi's Ageless Insight out, plus a tutor for Shark Typhoon in hand, but never drew a wheel. I dug 9-10 cards and found nothing, and the wheels were deep. I asked for research only, no swaps off one game.

First game on the newly sleeved v2.3.0. I found the wheels, got the commanders big and could have won. It still felt clunky and slow, brittle with nine mana and two taxes for the commanders, and the draw-and-discard was laborious. No result or table was logged.

Third game of an 0-3 night at Oliver's, the first on v3.0.0, against a bracket 3 table that is optimized to win around turn four. Oliver landed Krenko and the table asked me to kill it. I held Swords to Plowshares and a second removal spell, cast Shabraz instead, then passed another turn with mana open. Oliver went off for 30-plus damage in one turn. I called it entirely a piloting error, said it was the right hand misplayed, and asked for no deck changes.

read.what_it_does: On v3.0.0 it is meant to land Shabraz, grow him off card draw and a wheel, and win with a big flying shark through commander damage. One game has been played on this list, and it never got that far. Shabraz resolved, then I lost to Krenko before the plan could show anything (008). The plan itself is older than this list. Games on earlier versions got close the same way. A wheel made Shabraz big and almost killed Stuart through commander damage (001). In 006 I had Smothering Tithe with 36 Treasure, Fiery Emancipation and a tutor pointed at Shark Typhoon, and only the last piece was missing (006). Tithe, Typhoon and Emancipation are all still in the 99.
read.how_it_plays: Slow. I keep writing that (003, 005, 007), and the reason I give every time is the commanders: Brallin at four and Shabraz at five is nine mana, with a tax on top every time one gets removed (001, 005, 007). In 007, on v2.3.0, I found the wheels and could have won, and it still felt clunky, brittle and laborious (007). It survives a lot. In 006 it lived through several wipes and was beaten by a combo, not by damage (006). Every loss from 004 on went to a faster deck or a combo: Alex's warp turns (004), Purphoros pinging everyone (005), T'Vol going infinite on turn 8-9 (006) and Krenko for 30 in one turn (008). At Oliver's the bracket 3 decks are optimized and try to win around turn four (008), and this deck has not kept pace with that table yet. The wheels are loud, and the table either loves them or hates them (001, 002).
mindful_of: When the whole table names the threat and I'm holding the answer, use it. In 008 I held Swords to Plowshares and a second two-mana removal spell, cast Shabraz instead, then passed another turn with mana open, and Krenko killed me for 30-plus. I called it entirely a piloting error. Swords is still in the deck (008).
Kill on sight at Oliver's: Krenko (Oliver) and Purphoros (Tom). Early artifact removal on a Sol Ring opener is a fair play at that table (008). Purphoros also won the game in 005 (005).

Cast the first commander on curve. In 004 I held both back to dodge a wipe and waited for a wheel that never came, and that cost me the game's tempo (004). In 005 the commanders never came out at all (005).
Put resources into the commander line, not the small creatures. In 005 I got distracted by little discard creatures instead of getting a commander out and wheeling into it (005).

The wheel can be the missing piece. In 006 the board was set up and I dug 9-10 cards without finding one. After the game the first wheel was deep in the library (006). Know what the tutors fetch when the board has multipliers and no wheel.

Don't fire a wheel just to fire it. In 001 I threw away really useful cards of my own because I just needed to do the wheel (001). Wheels hit hardest as finishers, with both commanders out and already big (002).

Discarding without drawing back strands a small hand. Sitting on two or three cards, I didn't want to pay the discard (005). Forced discard felt like a cost in 006 and laborious in 007 (006, 007). v3.0.0 cut loot pieces, but no game has tested the change yet.
Commander tax piles up. Brallin was removed twice in 001 even with protection out (001). Swiftfoot Boots, which protected them in 001, is back in v3.0.0 (001).
Wheels cost goodwill. Making people discard their hand over and over is not something they enjoy (001, 002).
Downweight the goldfish on this deck. It doesn't see removal or interaction, and following it moves the deck in the wrong direction (002).
read.what_changed: v3.0.0 (Shabraz-first, merged and sleeved 2026-11-10) cut the wheel-and-burn engine from v2.3.0, including Marauding Mako, Glint-Horn Buccaneer, Psychosis Crawler and the loot spells. It added card draw to grow Shabraz, protection for when he lands (Swiftfoot Boots, Shelter, Slip Out the Back) and double strike. The one game on it (008) was lost to a misplay, and I asked for no deck changes, only more reps before any tuning. So nothing on this list is confirmed or refuted yet. The question it is meant to answer comes from 007, where v2.3.0 found its wheels and still felt clunky, slow and laborious (007). Older lessons that are superseded: the 'no removal' complaints in 001 and 003 were about lists before answers-v1 (v2.1.0) added interaction (001, 003). In 008 the removal was in hand, and I didn't use it (008). The 'too many wheels' read in 002 was on v1.3.0, and v2.0.0 cut wheels after it (002). Mystic Remora and Embercleave from 006, the Ledger and Bonnie/Annie loot pieces from 004 and Marauding Mako from 005 are on lists this deck no longer runs.
